name: Kettle
summary: A rocker switch that boils a kettle: bubbles climb, steam curls, it rattles and clicks off at 100°C
about: A boil switch for an electric kettle on a tiled kitchen counter. Flipping the rocker lights the base, and the water in the glass window warms from blue to orange: tiny bubbles cling to the bottom, then stream up and roll, steam curls out of the spout and the kettle rattles near the top. At 100°C a burst of steam lifts the lid and the switch clicks itself off, then the water slowly cools.
how: Press the Boil rocker (or Tab to it and press Space) to switch the kettle on.
Watch the temperature climb; it clicks off by itself at 100°C, or press again to stop early.
Pick 1 cup, 2 cups or Full to pour in fresh water; more water takes longer to boil.
Topping up while it heats mixes cold water in and drops the temperature.
